item.title: How Jensen Huang's return as NVIDIA's CEO is going over in China
item.description: In China, Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO is being met with a mixed reaction – as Beijing weighs whether it wants the US company's chips at all.
item.content:encoded: In China, Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO is being met with a mixed reaction – as Beijing weighs whether it wants the US company's chips at all.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia is in Spain after long-running deportation battle
item.description: Over the past year, the Trump administration sought to re-deport Kilmar Abrego Garcia, after immigration officials admitted that the first attempt was by mistake. On Tuesday, he self-deported to Spain

item.title: The White House is proposing new tariffs on more than a dozen countries
item.description: The White House is proposing new tariffs on goods from 14 of the U.S.'s biggest trading partners, including Japan, the EU and China – as high as 40% in China's case. Many of the details are unclear.

item.title: The west coast is bracing as some of the year's highest tides hit
item.description: Some of the highest tides of the year are happening this week on the West Coast. We hear about the impacts north of San Francisco and the additional king tides expected later this year.

item.title: What life is like in Kyiv under near-daily bombardments
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says his country has gathered intelligence on Russia's upcoming battle plans. The supposed goal of those plans: to make basic daily life in Kyiv impossible.

item.title: Teens from across the U.S. perform as the Macy's Great American Marching Band
item.description: Macy's is celebrating the 100th edition of its famous Thanksgiving Day Parade. We meet the students from around the country who join together to play in its signature marching band.

item.description: How did commercial airports get those three-letter codes — and why is Dulles known as IAD? An International Air Transport Association spokesperson helps explain.

item.title: Inflation is still hot, fueled in part by the AI boom
item.description: The U.S. economy grew at a rapid clip during the summer and early fall, due in part to the artificial intelligence boom. That boom is also fueling higher inflation and rattling the stock market.

item.title: With millions going home for Thanksgiving, it's the 'Super Bowl' of air travel
item.description: Winter storms are kicking up as tens of millions travel for the Thanksgiving holiday. People have braced for the worst but so far there have been few delays and cancelations.
